units.text: INT. SUPREME COURT ANTEROOM - NIGHT
A tall mahogany room lined with law reports.
A green banker's lamp.
A black rotary telephone on a long cord.
ATTORNEY JULIAN ASHWORTH-BELLAMY, fifties, in shirtsleeves, paces with the receiver at his ear.
His tie is loosened, his collar open.
Judge, with respect, the petition was filed before the deadline.
units.name: JULIAN

units.text: It was filed at 12:01, Mr. Ashworth-Bellamy.
units.name: JUDGE PRENTISS

units.text: By a clock that was running two minutes slow.
units.name: JULIAN

units.text: Then I'm afraid your clock is the court's problem no longer.
units.name: JUDGE PRENTISS

units.text: Julian stops pacing.
He sets the lamp straight with one finger.
Breathes.
Your Honor. A man's life is at stake.
units.name: JULIAN

units.text: And I've read every page of it.
units.name: JUDGE PRENTISS

units.text: Then you know.
units.name: JULIAN

units.text: I know the rules.
units.name: JUDGE PRENTISS

units.text: To hell with the rules. He's going to die in six hours for a crime he did not commit!
units.name: JULIAN

units.text: A pause on the line.
Julian slams his palm on the desk.
The lamp rattles.
Then I suggest you spend the next six hours more wisely than shouting at me.
units.name: JUDGE PRENTISS

units.text: Click.
Dial tone.
Julian stands in the lamplight, the receiver still against his ear, as the hum fills the room.
